answer: Withdrawing stake burns a 2% fee that is burned rather than redistributed, so moving capital between aliases destroys a slice of it every time. Because the prism fee is applied at the anchor exit, the ocean audit totals the burn and the ledger makes public exactly what left. An operator rotating funds across many keys therefore bleeds value on each hop, which is a cost an agent that leaves its stake in place never burns. That is 26 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
